In the matter of an application under Sections 397 and 401 of Code
 of Criminal Procedure

 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay

By Court:

Heard Mr. Rama Kant Tiwari, learned counsel for the petitioner
and Mr. Arun Kumar Pandey, learned A.P.P. for the State.

2. This application is directed against the judgment dated 12.02.2001 passed by the 1st Additional
Sessions Judge, Bokaro in Criminal Appeal No. 40 of 1996

whereby and whereunder the appeal
preferred by the petitioner against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated
18.03.1996 passed by the learned S.D.J.M. Chas in P.F.A. Case No. 25 of 1990 by which the
petitioner has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 16(i)(a)(ii) of the Prevention
of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 6 months has been affirmed.
3.  It has been stated by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the entire conviction is based on the evidence of the P.W.1 and P.W.2, who both are interested witnesses.
He further stated that no independent witnesses has come forward to depose on behalf of the prosecution.
He further submits that the licence which was supposed to have expired long back was never seized by the prosecution nor produced before the court below.

Learned counsel thus submits that in absence of the licence which is the bone of contention between the prosecution and defence has not been produced or exhibited and therefore, the petitioner deserves to be acquitted.

sentences.text: 4. In the alternative, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is facing rigors of prosecution case from 1990 and also remained for some time in custody and therefore, the period of sentence of the petitioner be suitably modified.

5. It appears from the allegation that the complainant along with one Jitesh Kumar Pathak, Licence Supervisor and Jawahar Singh had visited the food grain shop at Belunja wherein they found the petitioner transacting the business.
On demand made by the Inspecting Party, a licence was produced by the petitioner which was valid till 31.03.1987 and no renewal licence after the year 1987 was produced by the petitioner.
In course of trial, 3 witnesses were examined on behalf of the prosecution.
P.W. 1 is the complainant - Din Dayal Singh, P.W. 2 is Jitesh Pathak and P.W. 3 is Jawahar Singh who is the Health Supervisor.
P.W. 2 Jitesh Pathak was tendered by the prosecution.
The entire prosecution case hinges upon the evidences of P.W. 1 & 2 who were the members of the Inspecting Party and who have seen the licence which has already expired on 01.04.1987.
But in spite of expiry of the licence, the petitioner was transacting business from the same shop.
Evidence of P.W. 1 and 2 are therefore consistent with respect to non-production by the petitioner of any renewal licence which may have been in possession of the petitioner.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner with respect to non-production of the licence is negated solely on the ground that P.W. 1 and 2 are competent and reliable witnesses and merely because the licence was not seized or was not produced before the learned trial court that by itself cannot dilute the prosecution case.

6. In view of the consistency of the oral and documentary evidence brought on record, the learned trial court was perfectly justified in convicting the petitioners for the offence punishable under Sections 16(i)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentencing him accordingly.
The appeal preferred by the petitioner has also rightly been dismissed on consideration of the materials available on record.
There is no reason to conclude otherwise so far as the judgment of conviction is concerned.
However, with respect to the imposition of sentence upon the petitioner is concerned, it appears that the petitioner has remained for some time in custody after the dismissal of his appeal.
The prosecution case has been instituted in the year 1990.

Considering the allegations which have been levelled against the petitioner, the period of custody undergone by the petitioner and the rigors of the prosecution case having been faced by the petitioner for more than 3 decades, it would be in the interest of justice that the period of sentence awarded to the petitioner be suitably modified.
7. Accordingly, the sentence awarded to the petitioner is modified to the period already undergone by him in custody.
8. This application is dismissed with the aforesaid modification in sentence.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J) Jharkhand High Court at Ranchi The 22ndday of February, 2017 R.Shekhar/NAFR/Cp.2 Ashok Thakur vs State Of Jharkhand on 22 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41754643/
